description: Legacy-vs-extracted geometry parity using the REAL MSVC toolchain (VS2019 v142 / cl 19.29.30159 with atlmfc present) running under Wine. The unmodified legacy translation unit hammer/boundbox.cpp is compiled against the real mathlib/vector.h and linked with the extracted hammer::geometry::AxisAlignedBox; a driver asserts every observable operation is byte-identical in float arithmetic. This raises the Windows parity bar from 'MFC-free core cross-compiles and matches itself' (hammer_windows_parity.json, MinGW+Wine) to 'the extracted library reproduces the ACTUAL legacy code compiled by the ACTUAL Microsoft compiler'. The MSVC toolchain is a large licensed local install and is not a CI lane; the reproducible CI Windows lane remains MinGW-w64 + Wine (tools/quality/parity_wine.py).
compiler: Microsoft (R) C/C++ Optimizing Compiler Version 19.29.30159 for x64 (VS2019 v142, MSVCVER 14.29.30133, atlmfc present)
provisioning: mstorsjo/msvc-wine; MSVCVER pinned to 14.29.30133 (the toolset that ships atlmfc); SDK MSIs extracted with msitools/msiextract
note_on_defines: The msvc-wine cl wrapper mangles multiple command-line /D flags, so the Source platform define set (WIN32/_WIN32/WIN64/_WIN64/PLATFORM_64BITS/COMPILER_MSVC/COMPILER_MSVC64/NDEBUG) is supplied via a forced-include header (msvc_defines.h) instead. A case-alias stub 'BoundBox.h' resolves the legacy include spelling on a case-sensitive host.

positive.detail: legacy-vs-extracted BoundBox parity: all operations identical

negative.description: Mutant provider re-introduces the round-half-to-even (std::rint) bug in the extracted RoundHalfAwayFromZero, the exact fidelity regression found and fixed during extraction. The oracle must catch it.
negative.detail: FAIL SnapToGrid(16) .5-boundary: legacy mins(16,-16,0) vs extracted mins(0,0,0); FAIL SnapToGrid(8). 2 mismatches -> exit 1.

fidelityFinding: Legacy V_rint rounds half AWAY from zero (floor(f+0.5) for f>0, ceil(f-0.5) for f<0), NOT std::rint's round-half-to-even. RoundHalfAwayFromZero preserves this exactly; verified against the real V_rint compiled here verbatim (legacy_vrint.cpp) and against the real legacy Snap()/SnapToGrid path.
repro: scratchpad legacy-parity/run_legacy_parity.sh (positive + negative in one driver). Sources: unmodified hammer/boundbox.cpp, legacy_vrint.cpp (verbatim legacy V_rint), hammer/core/geometry/{aabb,rounding}.cpp, parity_boundbox.cpp.
scope: This verifies the extracted geometry LIBRARY against the real MSVC-compiled legacy code. It does NOT build the full MFC editor shell, which requires the entire Source Windows engine (tier0/vgui2/materialsystem import libs) and is tracked as out-of-scope for the extraction gate.

adapters.description: The single named owner of the Source-value boundary that both thin UI siblings (hammer.adapters.mfc, hammer.adapters.gtk) share. Proven under the same real MSVC/Wine lane that it lets a legacy BoundBox delegate geometry to the reusable library and get identical results (substitution guarantee), and that a broken seam is detected.

suites.detail: Real seam preserves legacy geometry: Vector<->Vec3 round-trip exact; op-on-legacy == ToAABB->op->FromAABB for SnapToGrid(16 .5-boundary)/SnapToGrid(8)/Rotate90(x,y,z).
Negative provider (BuggyAdapter swaps y/z into the library) is caught by 9 clauses; binary exits 0 meaning the seeded violation was correctly detected. Proves the seam oracle is sound.
